## Course Structure

This course consists of 10 sessions, each corresponding to one chapter. Sessions are grouped into three thematic parts that build on each other.

::: {.callout-box}
**Prerequisite chain:** Each chapter builds on the previous ones. It is strongly recommended to follow the chapters in order.
:::

## Part 1: Draw the Picture (Sessions 1--3)

| Session | Chapter | Topics | Preparation |
|---------|---------|--------|-------------|
| 1 | [Ch 1: Introduction to Causal Analysis](chapters/ch01.qmd) | Why causation matters; three traps (confounding, reverse causation, selection bias); basic DAGs | Read the pre-class essay |
| 2 | [Ch 2: Qualitative Causal Models](chapters/ch02.qmd) | Three node types; signed links; chains, forks, and colliders; information flow rules | Read the pre-class essay |
| 3 | [Ch 3: The MNH Diagnostic Case Study](chapters/ch03.qmd) | Building a DAG through interviews; root nodes as leverage points; supply vs. demand side | Read the pre-class essay |

## Part 2: Add the Numbers (Sessions 4--6)

| Session | Chapter | Topics | Preparation |
|---------|---------|--------|-------------|
| 4 | [Ch 4: Quantitative Causal Models](chapters/ch04.qmd) | Natural frequencies; lookup tables (CPTs); Bayes' rule with tree diagrams; Bayesian networks | Read the pre-class essay |
| 5 | [Ch 5: Situational Analysis](chapters/ch05.qmd) | Updating beliefs with evidence; explaining away; diagnosing problems from outcomes | Read the pre-class essay |
| 6 | [Ch 6: Simpson's Paradox & Cost-Effectiveness](chapters/ch06.qmd) | When combined data misleads; confounder vs. mediator; cross-country comparisons | Read the pre-class essay |

## Part 3: Make Decisions (Sessions 7--10)

| Session | Chapter | Topics | Preparation |
|---------|---------|--------|-------------|
| 7 | [Ch 7: Decision Analysis & Value of Information](chapters/ch07.qmd) | Decision maps; expected value; watching vs. doing; the value of running a pilot first | Read the pre-class essay |
| 8 | [Ch 8: Multi-Country Resource Allocation](chapters/ch08.qmd) | Three allocation strategies; uncertainty; Monte Carlo simulation; sequential decisions | Read the pre-class essay |
| 9 | [Ch 9: Game Theory & Strategic Interactions](chapters/ch09.qmd) | Payoff matrices; Nash equilibrium; the free-rider problem; commitment devices | Read the pre-class essay |
| 10 | [Ch 10: Structure Learning from Observational Data](chapters/ch10.qmd) | Can computers discover causes?; expert + algorithm; the feedback loop | Read the pre-class essay |

## Session Format

Each session follows a consistent structure:

1. **Concept presentation** — Core ideas explained with everyday analogies and MNH examples
2. **MNH application** — Real-world examples from Ethiopia, Rwanda, Kenya, and Tanzania
3. **R code workshop** — Hands-on coding with guided explanations
4. **Key takeaways and discussion** — Summary and preview of the next session

## Textbook

Ryall, M. D., & Bramson, A. (2014). *Inference and Intervention: Causal Models for Business Analysis*. Routledge.

The course teaches the same concepts from the textbook but uses entirely new examples drawn from public MNH data.
